description: A light, soft, pinkish-brown hardwood that peels well into large veneers. Mostly met as plywood, especially marine and boatbuilding plywood, and as blockboard and veneer.

hazards.summary: HSE lists asthma and cough among reported effects of gaboon (okoume). A wood-allergy review also lists it as a reported cause of occupational asthma, though the original case data were not available for checking.
HSE lists eye irritation from gaboon dust.
HSE lists skin effects, particularly on the hands and eyelids, from working with gaboon.
IARC classifies all wood dust as carcinogenic to humans, chiefly through cancers of the nose and sinuses. This applies to okoume dust as it does to any other wood.

image_prompt: Photorealistic studio photograph of a freshly planed okoume (Aucoumea klaineana) board, shot at a low three-quarter angle so the face grain fills most of the frame. Light pinkish-brown to salmon-colored heartwood, fairly even in tone, with slightly paler greyish sapwood at one edge. Straight to shallowly interlocked grain with a faint ribbon stripe, medium texture, and a soft silky luster. Soft diffused daylight from upper left, gentle falloff, neutral warm-grey seamless background, shallow depth of field with the near edge tack-sharp. No text, no logos, no hands, no tools, no finish or varnish, natural unfinished wood. Wide 1200x630 composition (1.91:1) with the board centered and margin on both sides for cropping.
image_alt: Planed board of okoume with even light pinkish-brown wood and a faint ribbon stripe.
notes_internal: Schlunssen-2018 lists 'Gaboon, Aucoumea spec.' with Kersten 1994 (Allergologie 17:55-60) only; not in PubMed/Crossref and not read. No PubMed primary report found for okoume asthma or dermatitis. Exposure is mostly via plywood, where glue resins add their own hazards. Slug 'okoume' chosen to avoid clash with 'Gaboon ebony' (Diospyros).
